name: National Bolshevism (NazBol)
summary: National Bolshevism is a syncretic current that fuses radical nationalism with Bolshevik-style socialism. Its adherents treat the nation as the highest value, want a revolution that nationalises industry and land under a planned economy, and look to Soviet Russia as an ally against the liberal, capitalist West and the Versailles order. Strands differ over democracy, race and religion.
scope: Weimar-era German National Bolshevism as set out in Karl Otto Paetel's 1933 manifesto for the Group of Social-Revolutionary Nationalists, with Ernst Niekisch's Widerstand circle and the Laufenberg-Wolffheim Hamburg group as its relatives. The 1990s-2000s Russian National Bolshevik Party of Limonov and Dugin is used only where it echoes the same positions. Excludes Strasserism, Ustryalov's Smena Vekh and later Western internet NazBol groups.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialized, nationally planned economy that treats welfare as a state task.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the pro-worker, anti-capitalist class-struggle stance.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Paetel vows to smash economic liberalism and replace the market with a socialist planned economy.

public-ownership.rationale: The Group's programme nationalises all large and medium industry and puts the means of production in common national property.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The programme goes far beyond taxation, to expropriation of large estates and nationalisation of industry, so higher taxes on the wealthy fit its direction.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are the revolutionary class and councils give them a voice, but the manifesto does not discuss trade unions as such.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme calls for severe class struggle against all who defend the sanctity of private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A state monopoly on foreign trade and nationalised industry mean tight control over, or replacement of, corporations.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; a socialist nation-building programme would not cut social provision, though it demands sacrifice from individuals.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership passes to the nation as common property rather than to each workforce, and Paetel is wary of interest-group control of the economy.

central-planning.rationale: The programme demands a socialist planned economy as the base of state sovereignty and a state monopoly on foreign trade.

socialized-markets.rationale: The model is a planned economy under national ownership, not market competition between public or worker firms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the programme declares the nation's ownership of land outright, which leaves little role for a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; the programme's expropriation of large estates implies hostility to inherited concentrations of wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; Paetel demands sacrifice of individual happiness and affluence for the community and ties rights to achievement.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programme calls for a state foreign-trade monopoly and autarchy as the goal, rejecting a world-mercantilist economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Planned national economy under state sovereignty, with nationalised industry and money.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme nationalises land and industry; only limited peasant smallholdings are granted, within socialist planning.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme nationalises the monetary system rather than abolishing money, and keeps a sovereign state and planned economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme calls for nationalising the monetary system, the opposite of leaving money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Paetel rejects the corporate state explicitly, arguing it perpetuates interest groups and reduces the state to a manufacturing company.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; individual rights are subordinated to the nation and the revolution, so security measures would be accepted.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the programme's ethos of sacrifice and discipline for the community.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is hostile to liberal speech rights yet its own volkisch language would be affected, so no clear answer can be inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Paetel wants a council-state with recallable delegates and leadership integrated into service, and rejects the Hitler model; Niekisch's strand was more authoritarian (s4).

state-harmful.rationale: The sovereign nation-state is the central instrument; the programme seeks a Greater-German council-state, not abolition of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: The programme demands arming the masses in a revolutionary people's militia, so private-gun limits are not a goal, but control would rest with the revolutionary state.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from the call for a revolutionary people's army and a military alliance with the USSR.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the stress on discipline and national sacrifice.

decide-locally.rationale: Councils are built from below as self-government, yet inside a unitary Greater-German state and sovereign nation, so adherents lean both ways.

rehabilitation.rationale: The vision includes People's Courts enforcing verdicts on enemies of the revolution; rehabilitation is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Not addressed by Paetel; the 1990s NBP programme sought to ban abortion and encourage births, pointing to a pro-family nationalism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the volkisch emphasis on the nation's biological and cultural continuity.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by Paetel; the first NBP programme (1994) sought an abortion ban, as reported by the 1990s scholarship cited.

more-religion-public.rationale: Paetel wants a new national faith (a neo-pagan 'new faith') to unify the Volk, but fights Christian and Roman influence and holds Marxist materialism; adherents split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an ethnic-national framing, though the manifesto rejects racial dogma as a foreign-policy criterion.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the volkisch emphasis on natural community and biological continuity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Paetel commits to the Volk as natural cultural community and to the intrinsic meaning of German folkdom, against Western civilisation.

gradual-change.rationale: Revolution is the path to the nation; Paetel calls for breaking with yesterday.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the ethnic-cultural conception of the Volk and the sovereignty stress.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement fights the Versailles order and treats internationality as the sum of national interests, rejecting supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: The programme demands a state foreign-trade monopoly and autarchy, and attacks world-mercantilist economy.

nation-first.rationale: The nation is the highest value in the manifesto, ahead of class, individual and humanity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the front against Western imperialism and the focus on national sovereignty tell against interventions in the name of human rights.

open-borders.rationale: The nation as the highest value and the community of sovereign socialist states leave no room for a borderless world.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the programme is built on state-led industrial socialism and Soviet-style development, not degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Jünger-style worker-and-technology ideas influenced the movement but with no clear thesis on progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the state-led industrialisation and national-strength priorities.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution is the path of the national-communist programme: the revolution of workers, peasants and the proletarianised middle class.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; councils are built from below, with recallable delegates earning workers' wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: Paetel's council-state breaks up the parties and has elected delegates; he also calls fascist corporatism a camouflaged dictatorship.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement is revolutionary and republican-minded, with a council-state replacing the dynastic Lander.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal parliamentary democracy is rejected as a Western system; Paetel offers council democracy as the 'old Germanic democracy' instead.

direct-votes.rationale: Council elections are explicitly indirect, rising from local councils to a national congress.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme's aim is the Free Greater-German People's Council-State, in which councils replace parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: The first NBP programme pledged to suppress ethnic minorities' separatism ruthlessly; Paetel replaces dynastic states with a single Greater-German council-state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Paetel rejects born-to-rule caste and master-race claims, but expects leaders to emerge by aptitude and achievement in an Order of the Nation.

political-violence-never.rationale: The programme calls for severe class struggle, a revolutionary militia, People's Courts and Saint-Just-style terror for the nation.

war-builds-character.rationale: Paetel rejects Jünger's justification of war as adventure; war is justified only by national need, not for its own sake.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programme struggles against Roman (Catholic) politics in Germany and wants the state sovereign, though it seeks a national faith.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Paetel attacks Christian influence, wants a 'new paganism' and a common law replacing Roman law, and treats ethics as subordinate to politics.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A sovereign revolutionary state and people's militia exclude private security and courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the call for a revolutionary people's army and a national-liberation foreign policy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Volk is defined as a natural ethnic-cultural community, though Paetel rejects race dogma and the NBP defines 'Russian' by culture, not blood (s3).

class-struggle-history.rationale: Paetel treats class struggle as a fact of social life and a recurrent replacement of leadership classes, though he subordinates it to the nation's struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Paetel ties the value of race and persons to achievement, not entitlement, and demands sacrifice of affluence for the community.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; the sovereign nation-state holds the land, which is declared national property.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from the movement's alliance with oppressed peoples and anti-colonial movements against the Versailles powers.

civilizational-union.rationale: The programme seeks a Russia-Germany economic region and a league of oppressed nations; the later NBP added a Eurasian empire (s3).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individual happiness is subordinated to the nation; Paetel demands sacrifice from the individual.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Paetel quotes Saint-Just and says rights are handed back to the nation when the Fatherland is in danger.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The 'new faith' invokes a cosmic religiosity centred on blood, soil and race, but nature's value is not discussed in policy terms.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; the later NBP programme sought mandatory births, suggesting a pro-natal stance.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement looks to Soviet industrial development and a planned economy, not a rejection of industrial civilisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; Niekisch looked to Soviet industrialisation, but no disruption-friendly view is documented.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the collectivist and volkisch emphasis.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the preference for council self-government of the Volk.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the subordination of individual rights to the nation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Paetel calls for breaking with yesterday while borrowing conservative-revolutionary ideas; the aim is new order, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The manifesto treats foreign policy as expediency, but it is strongly doctrinal on the nation and socialism.

direct-action.rationale: The programme seeks revolution rather than elections, and the later NBP used direct action such as occupying offices (s3).

means-match-ends.rationale: Paetel cites Saint-Just's terror and demands sacrifice of individual rights for the sake of the future community.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The programme is built on industrial socialism and a planned national economy.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The programme retains a planned industrial economy, with leaders and led by aptitude.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Paetel demands achievement as the measure of value and sacrifice for the nation; distribution by need is not stated.

production-for-use.rationale: A socialist planned economy replaces world-mercantilist economy so the economy serves the nation as a whole.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Paetel follows the Marxist account of the class struggle and the exploitative character of capitalist ownership.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The programme has People's Courts against the old regime and a revolutionary class struggle for workers' power, with the proletariat leading the nation.

collective-farming.rationale: Paetel wants to preserve the soil-bound peasant, with large estates expropriated and smallholdings given out.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The manifesto frames the world as a class struggle of nations against imperialist, capitalist powers.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme rejects the sanctity of property and puts economic resources at the nation's disposal.

harm-principle.rationale: Individual rights yield to the nation, the revolution and the community.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Paetel puts the nation first and says individual rights go back to the nation when it is in danger.

conscription.rationale: The revolutionary people's army (Volksheer) and the duty owed to the nation imply universal service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The nation as highest value makes leaving the community no solution; the programme demands commitment.

state-as-business.rationale: Paetel attacks the idea of the state as a manufacturing company and rejects the primacy of economic interests.

media-academia-power.rationale: Paetel treats press and cultural life as instruments of the class holding economic power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The manifesto rejects race dogma and a born-to-rule master race, though it uses volkisch racial language.

organic-representation.rationale: The councils break up parties and use workplace and residential districts, but Paetel explicitly rejects an estate-based corporate state.

total-state.rationale: Niekisch favoured a totalitarian state and Paetel subordinates individual and economic life to the nation, though through councils.

national-rebirth.rationale: The manifesto's task is to 'become a Nation', breaking with the decadent past through revolution and a new faith.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The vision marches a socialist Greater Germany over the Rhine and the Eastern settlement programme; Paetel rejects colonies, so expansion is continental.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on a council constitution; the Order of the Nation is bound by voluntary allegiance, not lord-vassal feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The programme expropriates large estates and gives land to peasants, the reverse of bonding labor to a lord.

universal-morality.rationale: Paetel says politics has its own laws and ethics no business in it, and grounds values in the Volk.

single-common-good.rationale: The council-state is meant to express the nation's unity as a volonte generale, not interest-group party competition.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; Paetel's 1933 text expects Jews to emigrate or integrate as a national minority without addressing Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The first NBP programme sought to unite all Russians in one state, with territories annexed where Russians are the majority.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Councils are elected in the workplace as the basis of the state, though ownership belongs to the nation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the planned, national approach to society.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the programme's nationalised monetary system and state-directed economy.

economic-freedom.rationale: Paetel wants to smash economic liberalism and free the economy for the nation, not individuals.

rule-by-example.rationale: The programme relies on People's Courts, a militia and law, with leaders chosen by performance.

national-self-determination.rationale: The whole programme is a fight for German sovereignty against Versailles, allied with all oppressed peoples' freedom movements.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary foreign policy and the view that Versailles-era institutions are illegitimate.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Paetel calls for a new faith of blood and soil and rejects free-thinking 'pseudo-enlightenment', though his Marxist side wants irrationalism overcome.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed by Paetel; the 1990s NBP put the nation's rights before individual rights, implying citizens first.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the ethos of duty and the labour-based franchise of the council system.

class-collaboration.rationale: Paetel calls the class struggle a fact and demands a stated choice of side.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Paetel breaks with yesterday politically but keeps culture as the nation's 'golden core' of inherited treasures.

dominated-front.rationale: Paetel demands a front against Versailles and the West, allied with Russia and all oppressed peoples.

workers-nation.rationale: Paetel commits to the nation as the last political value and has the proletariat build the nation, in contrast to Marxist internationalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Paetel's socialist demand for a nationalised, planned economy that frees a proletarianized people from material bondage.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The sources do not address it and the strands split, with Paetel's circle silent and later groups mixing traditional and egalitarian stances.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialised planned economy that leaves lending to the state rather than banning interest by law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Paetel treats Volk and race as natural facts but rejects racial doctrines as a program and builds on the nation, not state-enforced separation; later groups differ, so this is inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Paetel accepts that class struggle is a fact reflected in state, press and culture, though he wants the state to become the sovereign nation's instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the aim of a nationally planned, self-sufficient economy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed in the manifesto; inferred from its nation-first stance, and the Russian party's emphasis on titular nations.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not addressed; the manifesto's enemy is Western liberal capitalism and Versailles rather than a secret plan by elites.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's rejection of the Weimar parliamentary party system in favor of revolutionary national socialism.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred: the manifesto seeks a front of oppressed nations against the West, each finding its own path, rather than exporting a model.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nationalist outlook that gives no priority to sex-based hierarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Paetel condemns the Weimar system and its parties as failing the nation and the workers.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: Niekisch opposed Nazi racial biology and the movement was not built on eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from revolutionary nationalism that places the nation's needs above legal restraint on the state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Paetel vows to smash economic liberalism and put a planned, socialized national economy in its place.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Adherents split: Paetel rejected race dogma, while the later Russian party stressed titular nations; inferred, not addressed directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto tying worth to achievement and service to the nation, and organizing society by aptitude of leaders and led.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Inferred: the movement seeks a national socialism for each nation on its own path, allied with others, rather than waiting for revolution abroad.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from its alliance of oppressed nations against the West; settlement displacing a people is not directly addressed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from a sovereign, planned national state with a single legal order; not addressed directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between a new national faith hostile to Christian and Roman influence and tolerance of religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Paetel's neo-pagan, volkisch orientation which sees no sacred cattle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the programme's struggle against Roman Catholic political influence and a sovereign national state.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from the sovereign, totalitarian-leaning state of Niekisch and Paetel facing a hostile Western order.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Council democracy rooted in the people suggests some consent, but liberal consent is rejected; adherents split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred: the Marxist strand reads ideas as class-bound and the manifesto rejects liberal Western universalism as a tool of the Versailles powers.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred: a nationalised planned economy aimed at national independence from the capitalist West points to autarkic, export-minded policy; the sources do not state it.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred: the Paetel manifesto rejects racial exclusion, though other strands, such as the Russian party's titular-nation line, are harsher toward minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement aims at violent revolution and a militant nationalist state, so a ban on initiating force is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: struggle between nations and a revolutionary national will are central, but its Marxist side stresses class rather than competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: an authoritarian council-state would not tolerate parties seeking to abolish it, and Niekisch had totalitarian leanings.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred: its core grievance is domination of the nation by Versailles and Western capital, and it holds workers unfree under capitalist power.

separated-powers.rationale: The manifesto's council-state and the movement's authoritarian leanings reject liberal checks and balances.

vanguard-party.rationale: Inferred: it was an elite revolutionary minority that expected to lead the nation, but it framed the leader as the nation, not the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: It demands nationalising industry and land under a planned economy in the interest of the labouring nation.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nationalised, planned economy that keeps major assets in public hands.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the nation-first council state and Niekisch's authoritarian leanings, which subordinate industrial action to national needs.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the socialist view that property relations, not numbers, cause want.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Strands split: Paetel rejects racism, while the later Russian party stressed titular nations; no single line can be sourced.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: the manifesto calls for a revolutionary elite and council-state, not chance selection.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary dictatorial state sought by the movement and Niekisch's totalitarian leanings.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from the planned socialist economy it demands.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Paetel treating the press as a class instrument and from the authoritarian revolutionary state.

party-commands-army.rationale: Inferred from the Bolshevik-style revolutionary movement and its call for a people's army of the revolution.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its nation-first stance and the Russian party's emphasis on titular nations.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the anti-capitalist, socialist council-state in Paetel's manifesto, which treats office as service to the nation.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Inferred: a revolutionary movement that wants disciplined action behind a common programme, though Niekisch-type circles stressed loyalty to a cause over formal party rules.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Paetel's manifesto puts national sovereignty first and sets the movement against the Versailles order and the Western liberal powers, so a binding supranational union runs against it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; the manifesto favours a council-state, but Niekisch's circle leaned toward an authoritarian state, so strands split on strong executive command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred: the strands are not clerical and the manifesto treats religion as secondary to the nation, so an episcopal church governed from above is not a goal.

clerical-rule.rationale: Paetel's programme is a secular national-socialist council-state with the nation as the highest value, leaving no room for clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred: the movement puts the nation first and wants to wage war against the Versailles order, so it would not call for its own country's defeat, though it admired the Soviet side.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; strands split between a revolutionary cultural avant-garde and authoritarian cultural policy.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; the Weimar strands were opposed to the parliamentary republic and offered no settled rule on terms for a leader.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from the council-state model Paetel proposes, which rests on accountable delegates, though the manifesto gives no recall rule.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: Paetel's front against the West and Versailles order rejects Western alliances, though it seeks an alliance with Russia.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialized economy that nationalizes land and industry rather than spreading private ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a revolutionary nationalism that may favor a people's militia, but the strands also back strong states and armies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist strands idealize peasant and soil-rooted community, though the movement is mainly urban and revolutionary.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Both the Weimar nationalists against Versailles and the Russian National Bolsheviks demand that divided national territory and ethnic compatriots be brought into one state.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: the movement's populist, anti-establishment stance fits distrust of university-trained elites.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: its nationalism and civilizational thinking favor the national culture's distinct worth, not strict equality of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian leanings and a combative nationalism point to support for harsh penalties, though no source states it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: its nationalist, traditionalist strands oppose liberal gender education in schools.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: the Bolshevik side is secular and materialist, but the movement spans religious and atheist strands, so the answer is weak.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred: nationalist and authoritarian strands oppose cultural decadence, though no source addresses it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from its nation-first and ethnic-nation position, which favors membership of the people by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Rogatchevski shows the Russian strand privileges the titular nation over ethnic minorities, so minority-language support is unlikely.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from a nation-first stance that treats common national law as binding on all.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: Paetel's discipline-minded national collective leaves little room for celebrating eccentric ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rejection of the Versailles order and its reparations and from solidarity with oppressed peoples.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Paetel ties national liberation to a socialist revolution that nationalises industry and land.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the council-state model and hostility to Weimar parliamentarism.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Strands lean authoritarian, and Niekisch is described as totalitarian in his leanings.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the nation as the highest value; aid abroad is not part of the programme.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the demand for full national sovereignty against the West.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the council-state and authoritarian leanings favor leadership by revolutionary bodies over popular election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A nationalised, planned economy implies government direction of money.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from radical nationalism, which treats national territory as inalienable.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The programme nationalises industry and land and subordinates ownership to the nation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Paetel and Niekisch looked to Soviet Russia as a socialist ally against the West.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from a nationally planned economy that subordinates private interest to the nation; not addressed in the manifesto.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred: Paetel sought alliance with Soviet Russia and a front against the Western powers, so binding alliances are acceptable.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: rejection of Versailles treats imposed territorial changes as illegitimate; Russian National Bolsheviks make similar claims about lost territories.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Strands differ on religion, so adherents are split; the state-above-church view is only inferred from the primacy of the nation.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects parliamentary parties and favors a revolutionary national leadership, not a neutral figurehead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from treating the nation as the highest political value, and the militarism of Limonov's party.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred: a planned, nationalized economy under a national state implies one system across the territory.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: a Bolshevik-style revolutionary movement is secular and has no divine kingship.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: a socialist planned economy implies progressive taxation rather than a flat rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Strands differ on race and nature versus nurture, so adherents are split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: a revolution against Weimar legality and liberalism sees the revolutionary power as above inherited law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows from the nation-first socialism of the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: opposes parliamentary democracy and seeks unified national leadership.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from calls for strong leadership and the leader-centred style of Limonov's party.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; no position follows from the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the nation as a unity above classes and from socialism understood as a national task.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Paetel programme looks to nationalised industry and land under a planned economy, so taking estates from owners fits.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's rejection of the Versailles order and its concern for the nation, including Germans cut off by the new borders.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Revolt against the post-1919 borders and the later Russian party's claims for Russians left outside Russia make irredentism central.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; the German strand had a neo-pagan wing and the Russian party was secular, so criminalising leaving a faith is not part of it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Bolshevik-style secular socialism and a cultural nation, which has no place for religious dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its anti-Western, anti-liberal stance and its focus on national sovereignty and autarky.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from the Russian strand's drive to reunite Russians across the post-Soviet borders and the German strand's eastern, Slavic-friendly orientation.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the nation-first, unitary outlook, in which minorities rank below the titular nation.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the principle that every nation needs its own state and homeland, so a persecuted people building one fits better than staying.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from a nationalism that gives primacy to the nation and to will over economic determinism, though its socialism is Bolshevik.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a planned, nationalised economy in which the state directs industry rather than policing market competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a planned economy under national control, in which the state keeps national industry going rather than leaving it to fail.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from the anti-liberal, council-state and authoritarian leanings of the movement, which distrust independent institutions that block the national will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a Volkisch, nation-centred outlook with no stated equality-quota policy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the front against the Western powers, an alliance with Russia and the call for a nationally planned economy outside liberal world trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the view of Western-led trade regimes as tools of domination; binding external standards would erode national sovereignty.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the call for the nation as the last political value, which asks for service and sacrifice beyond personal gain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from the call for a revolution led by an activist minority of social-revolutionary nationalists, and the Russian party's direct-action style.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from its revolutionary-socialist call to overturn old elites, though Niekisch's circle admired Prussian tradition.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a doctrine that makes the nation the last political value and stresses national tradition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the call for a common front of oppressed peoples against the Western powers.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Paetel's commitment to the nation as the highest political value.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, since strands differ over race and the Russian party favoured titular nations while the Weimar current was not racial.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialized, nationally planned economy that would place credit under state control.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the revolutionary anti-capitalist stance that sought to overthrow the system.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from the Russian National Bolsheviks' claims on former Soviet lands, though the Weimar current had no such empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western stance and the call for national economic independence from the liberal world order.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, since the nation-first view treats workers as part of the nation and rejects an international class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a socialized economy under which private owners lack such freedom of dealing.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rejection of liberal parliamentarism in favour of a national revolution.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The movement rejected Versailles as a dictated peace that divided Germans without their consent.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not a monarchist current and wanted a leader drawn from the national movement; whether by election is contested, inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: The nation is placed above the individual, so no member can hold a veto; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A revolutionary current that rejected the legitimacy of the Weimar order; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: National Bolshevists rejected Weimar parliamentary democracy and the Western liberal order.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No documented position; adherents are not committed either way.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No documented position; inferred from conventional practice among adherents.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Anti-bourgeois and socialist, it replaces paternal duty with national solidarity and public ownership; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: A revolutionary activist movement that demanded total political commitment.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Hostile to Western liberal capitalist culture as corrosive; inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Treats the bourgeois order as rule by capital and force, which revolution must overthrow; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Casts the Western capitalist powers as exploiting Germany and Russia through Versailles and the world market.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nationalist currents, including Limonov's party, favor titular nations over ethnic minorities.

party-own-road.rationale: Looks to Soviet Russia as ally but wants a national road to socialism; inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Niekisch's circle favored autarky and an eastward alliance against Western capital; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revision of Versailles and recovery of lost lands are central, and Limonov's party demanded Russian territories back.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: By analogy to titular-nation preference over minorities; inferred.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The current rejects the liberal-democratic constitution this value presupposes, though it opposed Hitler's regime in places; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Admired the Soviet system and drew on both left and right, so it rejects condemning them together; inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; the socialist side of the doctrine implies slavery was central; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Emphasis on national tradition suggests keeping national symbols; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Traditionalist, soldierly outlook; not documented, inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: No documented stance and the strands split between egalitarian-socialist and traditionalist views.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rejects Western liberal institutions as alien and promotes a distinct Eastern or national path, as in Niekisch and Dugin.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Niekisch's Prussian soldierly ideal and Limonov's militarism favor a political role for the military; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: No documented stance; adherents split between socialist and traditionalist views.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nation-first outlook that values the community's bonds across generations.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the manifesto favours a council-state led by a revolutionary elite rather than examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The manifesto wants nationalised industry and a struggle against Western capital, which excludes foreign takeovers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nationalist outlook that values the family.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the council-state model, in which delegates answer to those who chose them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: a planned, nationalised economy leaves no room for private pension accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme nationalises land and holds it for the nation.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: the manifesto rejects liberal parliamentarism in favour of a council-state.

single-official-language.rationale: The Russian National Bolshevik programmes favour the titular nation's language and culture, though the German strand is not clear on it.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from a nationalist programme that keeps national land in national hands.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the programmes put the nation first and treat outcome-based discrimination claims as foreign to this stance.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of Western liberal capitalism and its materialist culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the call for a revolutionary front with Russia and oppressed peoples against the West.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; Soviet-aligned strands might approve while the nation-first outlook opposes dominating others.

missingStatements.text: Countries that see themselves as dominated by the leading Western powers should form a common front against them.
missingStatements.rationale: Paetel's revolutionary foreign policy is a front against Versailles and the West, allied with Russia and all oppressed peoples.

missingStatements.text: The working class should organize along national lines rather than as an international class.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining claim is that socialism needs the nation: Paetel commits to the nation as the last political value, and the KPD's Radek and Thalheimer rejected National Bolshevism for putting nation first.

notes: The German strand used here is anti-Nazi and anti-fascist in its own words but is Volkisch, with a neo-pagan religious wing; Niekisch's circle was more authoritarian and Prussian-minded. The 1994 Russian programme was openly illiberal and total-statist, and was moderated to a liberal 'minimum programme' in 2004 (s3), so many answers differ by strand. The Russian party's definition of nation was cultural, not racial.
